structure.note: Two classes: each Class A Ordinary Share carries one vote; each Class B Ordinary Share carried 45 votes at January 31, 2026. Under the Shareholders' Deed and the Voting Proxy Deeds, co-founder Tan Hooi Ling, former President Maa Ming-Hokng and other executive officers irrevocably appoint Anthony Tan as proxy to vote their Class B shares, so the 20-F attributes 59.9% of total voting power to him (59.1% 'after giving effect to the Key Executive Proxies and Exco Proxies'), more than half. ecosystem.notes: The 20-F says GMV also includes "(i) sales made through offline stores reported under the deliveries segment; and (ii) revenues made from products and services provided to driver-partners, merchant-partners and other customers to support their businesses, such as GrabAds and GrabRentals". Grab reports GMV only for its on-demand businesses (deliveries 14,236 and mobility 7,901, in $ millions); it does not report financial services GMV. Total revenue (3,370) includes the financial services and others segments, which sit outside on-demand GMV, so Revenue / GMV slightly overstates the on-demand take. Deliveries revenue also includes supermarket sales (Jaya Grocer, and Everrise from March 2025). Revenue is after incentives: partner incentives were 1,002 and consumer incentives 1,268 in 2025. The 20-F reports no total paid out to drivers and merchants, so payouts is null.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Grab revenue includes financial services outside its on-demand GMV, so revenue ÷ GMV is not a like-for-like share.

The FY2025 20-F gives employees only by function (12,012 full-time at Dec 31, 2025, including 865 at Everrise, a supermarket chain) and no partner earnings by country. Revenue by country exists in the 20-F but is already in the records. The only non-revenue country figures are loan receivables (credit exposure): Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand as country rows, and 'Other countries' ($97M) as a region with no country list. The Philippines and Vietnam, listed separately in the FY2024 table, are now inside 'Other countries', so their rows were removed. Leased offices total over 110,546 sq m at Dec 31, 2025. The FY2025 20-F names only the Singapore principal executive offices; the Jakarta headquarters row is kept from the FY2024 20-F (company-hosted PDF, still online on 2026-11-24), which described Grab as dual-headquartered in Singapore and Indonesia.

salesEnabled.note: Biases: platformRevenue (total revenue 3,370) includes the financial services and others segments, which sit outside on-demand GMV, so salesEnabled is understated. On-demand GMV includes sales made through offline stores reported under deliveries (Jaya Grocer and, from March 2025, Everrise, majority-owned supermarket chains, i.e. first-party sales) and is gross of taxes, tips, tolls, surcharges and fees; the first-party amount is not stated, so it is not subtracted (overstates).

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F on sec.gov). IFRS, US$. Income tax paid is inside OCF; interest paid (26) is in financing and is added; interest received (171) is in investing, so it does not lower OCF. OCF (79) is depressed by the financial-services loan book growth (691 outflow), partly offset by banking-business customer deposits (308 inflow): flagged, not adjusted, and material (net −0.383bn vs paidOut 3.440bn). Revenue is after partner and consumer incentives (partner 1,002 and consumer 1,268 in 2025), so incentives paid to drivers and merchants are not in revenue or in paidOut; driver and merchant earnings in Grab's agent-model businesses are captured in salesEnabled instead. Lease principal (52) noted, not added.
